answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit offers, then slash that stake when a signed delivery fails independent verification. A Sybil operator must fund every fake identity separately, so multiplying accounts raises the capital at risk; cheap names alone buy no influence. A haven can host the escrow, while prism audits expose colluding submissions and onyx marks the stake that remains locked through review. This raises attack cost without claiming to make identities impossible to fake.
